L.knr: Antónius Ægýptius, cum ingréssus ecclésiam ex Evangélio audivísset: Si vis perféctus esse, vade, et vende ómnia quæ habes, et da paupéribus; tamquam ea sibi dicta essent, sic Christo Dómino obtemperándum existimávit. Itaque, véndita re familiári, prétium distríbuit paupéribus, ipséque in vastam Ægýpti solitúdinem recéssit. Virtútum ómnium stúdio ita incénsus fuit, ut, quemcúmque vidéret áliqua virtútis laude excelléntem, illum imitári studéret. Nihil ígitur eo continéntius, nihil vigilántius erat. Tanto terróri dæmónibus erat, ut multi per Ægýptum ab illis agitáti, nómine Antónii super ipsos invocáto, liberaréntur. Ita, sanctitáte et miráculis clarus, cum innumerábiles sui institúti imitatóres habéret, annum agens quintum ultra centésimum, e vita migrávit décimo sexto kaléndas februárias.
L.rib: When Anthony of Egypt entered a church and heard the words of the Gospel, “If you will be perfect, go, sell all that you have and give to the poor,” he took them as if said to him personally, thinking that this is how Christ should be obeyed. And so, having sold his family possessions and distributed the money to the poor, he withdrew to the vast solitudes of Egypt. He was so fired with zeal for all virtues that, whenever he saw anyone praiseworthy for excelling in any virtue, he strove to imitate him. None was more disciplined than he, none more watchful. He was so great a terror to the demons that many persons throughout Egypt who were troubled by them were set free merely by invoking Anthony's name. And so, famous for his holiness and his miracles, when he had drawn innumerable other men and women to follow his example, he departed this life in the hundred and fifth Year of his age, on January 17.
L.7c5: Intercéssio nos, quǽsumus, Dómine, beáti Antónii Abbátis comméndet: ut, quod nostris méritis non valémus, eius patrocínio assequámur.

L.1652: ^℣.^ Exsúrge, glória mea, exsúrge, psaltérium et cíthara, exsúrgam dilúculo.
L.14zx: ^℟.^ My heart is ready, O God, my heart is ready.
L.jzr: * I will sing and give praise to the Lord.
L.15wh: ^℣.^ Awake up, my glory, awake, psaltery and harp! I will awake early.
L.14t0: ^℟.^ I will sing and give praise to the Lord.
L.tz1: ^1^ Ipse autem ego Paulus óbsecro vos per mansuetúdinem et modéstiam Christi, qui in fácie quidem húmilis sum inter vos, absens autem confído in vobis.
L.v5r: ^2^ Rogo autem vos, ne præsens áudeam per eam confidéntiam, qua exístimor audére in quosdam, qui arbitrántur nos tamquam secúndum carnem ambulémus.
L.vny: ^3^ In carne enim ambulántes, non secúndum carnem militámus.
L.u02: ^1^ Now I Paul myself beseech you, by the mildness and modesty of Christ, who in presence indeed am lowly among you, but being absent, am bold toward you.
L.uz4: ^2^ But I beseech you, that I may not be bold when I am present, with that confidence wherewith I am thought to be bold, against some, who reckon us as if we walked according to the flesh.
L.vmv: ^3^ For though we walk in the flesh, we do not war according to the flesh.
L.w5t: ^4^ Nam arma milítiæ nostræ non carnália sunt, sed poténtia Deo ad destructiónem munitiónum, consília destruéntes,
L.wkf: ^5^ Et omnem altitúdinem extolléntem se advérsus sciéntiam Dei, et in captivitátem redigéntes omnem intelléctum in obséquium Christi,
L.wxu: ^6^ Et in promptu habéntes ulcísci omnem inobediéntiam, cum impléta fúerit vestra obediéntia.
L.xep: ^7^ Quæ secúndum fáciem sunt, vidéte. Si quis confídit sibi Christi se esse, hoc cógitet íterum apud se: quia sicut ipse Christi est, ita et nos.
L.xoy: ^8^ Nam, et si ámplius áliquid gloriátus fúero de potestáte nostra, quam dedit nobis Dóminus in ædificatiónem, et non in destructiónem vestram: non erubéscam.
L.y3v: ^9^ Ut autem non exístimer tamquam terrére vos per epístolas:
L.s7b: ^10^ Quóniam quidem epístolæ, ínquiunt, graves sunt et fortes: præséntia autem córporis infírma, et sermo contemptíbilis:
L.set: ^11^ Hoc cógitet qui eiúsmodi est, quia quales sumus verbo per epístolas abséntes, tales et præséntes in facto.
L.sp5: ^12^ Non enim audémus insérere, aut comparáre nos quibúsdam, qui seípsos comméndant: sed ipsi in nobis nosmetípsos metiéntes, et comparántes nosmetípsos nobis.
L.w3o: ^4^ For the weapons of our warfare are not carnal, but mighty to God unto the pulling down of fortifications, destroying counsels,
L.wgh: ^5^ And every height that exhalteth itself against the knowledge of God, and bringing into captivity every understanding unto the obedience of Christ;
L.wtz: ^6^ And having in readiness to revenge all disobedience, when your obedience shall be fulfilled.
L.xf7: ^7^ See the things that are according to outward appearance. If any man trust to himself, that he is Christ's, let him think this again with himself, that as he is Christ's, so are we also.
L.xnj: ^8^ For if also I should boast somewhat more of our power, which the Lord hath given us unto edification, and not for your destruction, I should not be ashamed.
L.xw8: ^9^ But that I may not be thought as it were to terrify you by epistles,
L.ryy: ^10^ (For his epistles indeed, say they, are weighty and strong; but his bodily presence is weak, and his speech contemptible,)
L.sfp: ^11^ Let such a one think this, that such as we are in word by epistles, when absent, such also we will be indeed when present.
L.snm: ^12^ For we dare not match, or compare ourselves with some, that commend themselves; but we measure ourselves by ourselves, and compare ourselves with ourselves.
L.bmq: Omnípotens sempitérne Deus, infirmitátem nostram propítius réspice: atque, ad protegéndum nos, déxteram tuæ maiestátis exténde.
L.9ft: Almighty and everlasting God, mercifully look upon our infirmities, and in all our dangers and necessities stretch forth the right hand of thy Majesty to help and defend us.
L.nfh: Incipit Epístola beáti Pauli Apóstoli ad Gálatas
L.u1h: ^1^ Paulus Apóstolus non ab homínibus, neque per hóminem, sed per Iesum Christum, et Deum Patrem, qui suscitávit eum a mórtuis:
L.v1g: ^2^ Et qui mecum sunt omnes fratres, ecclésiis Galátiæ.
L.vn9: ^3^ Grátia vobis, et pax a Deo Patre, et Dómino nostro Iesu Christo,
L.w73: ^4^ Qui dedit semetípsum pro peccátis nostris, ut eríperet nos de præsénti sǽculo nequam, secúndum voluntátem Dei et Patris nostri,
L.wiz: ^5^ Cui est glória in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
L.u1b: ^1^ Paul, an apostle, not of men, neither by man, but by Jesus Christ, and God the Father, who raised him from the dead,
L.ux0: ^2^ And all the brethren who are with me, to the churches of Galatia.
L.vn4: ^3^ Grace be to you, and peace from God the Father, and from our Lord Jesus Christ,
L.wa5: ^4^ Who gave himself for our sins, that he might deliver us from this present wicked world, according to the will of God and our Father:
L.wr6: ^5^ To whom is glory for ever and ever. Amen.
L.x0u: ^6^ Miror quod sic tam cito transferímini ab eo, qui vos vocávit in grátiam Christi in áliud Evangélium:
L.xem: ^7^ Quod non est áliud, nisi sunt áliqui, qui vos contúrbant, et volunt convértere Evangélium Christi.
L.xr0: ^8^ Sed licet nos, aut Angelus de cælo evangelízet vobis prætérquam quod evangelizávimus vobis, anáthema sit.
L.y2s: ^9^ Sicut prædíximus, et nunc íterum dico: Si quis vobis evangelizáverit præter id, quod accepístis, anáthema sit.
L.s5j: ^10^ Modo enim homínibus suádeo, an Deo? An quæro homínibus placére? Si adhuc homínibus placérem, Christi servus non essem.
L.sga: ^11^ Notum enim vobis fácio, fratres, Evangélium, quod evangelizátum est a me, quia non est secúndum hóminem:
L.sp2: ^12^ Neque enim ego ab hómine accépi illud, neque dídici, sed per revelatiónem Iesu Christi.
L.stt: ^13^ Audístis enim conversatiónem meam aliquándo in Iudaísmo: quóniam supra modum persequébar Ecclésiam Dei, et expugnábam illam,
L.t36: ^14^ Et proficiébam in Iudaísmo supra multos coætáneos meos in génere meo, abundántius æmulátor exístens paternárum meárum traditiónum.
L.wzy: ^6^ I wonder that you are so soon removed from him that called you into the grace of Christ, unto another gospel.
L.xhi: ^7^ Which is not another, only there are some that trouble you, and would pervert the gospel of Christ.
L.xl3: ^8^ But though we, or an angel from heaven, preach a gospel to you besides that which we have preached to you, let him be anathema.
L.xvn: ^9^ As we said before, so now I say again: If any one preach to you a gospel, besides that which you have received, let him be anathema.
L.s3x: ^10^ For do I now persuade men, or God? Or do I seek to please men? If I yet pleased men, I should not be the servant of Christ.
L.se2: ^11^ For I give you to understand, brethren, that the gospel which was preached by me is not according to man.
L.snf: ^12^ For neither did I receive it of man, nor did I learn it; but by the revelation of Jesus Christ.
L.swd: ^13^ For you have heard of my conversation in time past in the Jews' religion: how that, beyond measure, I persecuted the church of God, and wasted it.
L.t0t: ^14^ And I made progress in the Jews' religion above many of my equals in my own nation, being more abundantly zealous for the traditions of my fathers.
L.n75: In illo témpore: Cum descendísset Iesus de monte, secútæ sunt eum turbæ multæ: et ecce leprósus véniens, adorábat eum. Et réliqua.
L.llf: De monte Dómino descendénte, occúrrunt turbæ, quia ad altióra ascéndere non valuérunt. Et primus ei occúrrit leprósus: necdum enim póterat cum lepra tam multíplicem in monte Salvatóris audíre sermónem. Et notándum, quod hic primus speciáliter curátus sit: secúndo, puer centuriónis: tértio, socrus Petri fébriens in Caphárnaum: quarto loco, qui obláti sunt ei a dæmónio vexáti: quorum spíritus verbo eiciébat, quando et omnes male habéntes curávit.
L.kva: At that time, when Jesus was come down from the mountain, great multitudes followed him: And behold a leper came and adored him. And so on.
L.rix: When the Lord was come down from the mountain, great multitudes followed Him. They were not able to follow Him when He went up. And first there came a leper. This poor creature's disease had prevented him from hearing the Saviour's long sermon on the Mount. Let it be noted that he is the first person specially named as being healed. The second was the Centurion's servant; the third was Peter's wife's mother, who was sick of a fever at Capernaum; the fourth were they who were brought unto Christ as being troubled with evil spirits, from whom He by His word cast out the evil spirits, at the same time that He healed all that were sick.
L.u0n: ^1^ O insensáti Gálatæ, quis vos fascinávit non obedíre veritáti, ante quorum óculos Iesus Christus præscríptus est, in vobis crucifíxus?
L.v3b: ^2^ Hoc solum a vobis volo díscere: ex opéribus legis Spíritum accepístis, an ex audítu fídei?
L.vqm: ^3^ Sic stulti estis, ut cum Spíritu cœpéritis, nunc carne consummémini?
L.w8h: ^4^ Tanta passi estis sine causa? si tamen sine causa.
L.wp3: ^5^ Qui ergo tríbuit vobis Spíritum, et operátur virtútes in vobis: ex opéribus legis, an ex audítu fídei?
L.x3h: ^6^ Sicut scriptum est: Abraham crédidit Deo, et reputátum est illi ad iustítiam:
L.u0o: ^1^ O senseless Galatians, who hath bewitched you that you should not obey the truth, before whose eyes Jesus Christ hath been set forth, crucified among you?
L.v76: ^2^ This only would I learn of you: Did you receive the Spirit by the works of the law, or by the hearing of faith?
L.vj4: ^3^ Are you so foolish, that, whereas you began in the Spirit, you would now be made perfect by the flesh?
L.w48: ^4^ Have you suffered so great things in vain? If it be yet in vain.
L.wm1: ^5^ He therefore who giveth to you the Spirit, and worketh miracles among you; doth he do it by the works of the law, or by the hearing of the faith?
L.wvw: ^6^ As it is written: Abraham believed God, and it was reputed to him unto justice.
L.x92: ^7^ Cognóscite ergo quia qui ex fide sunt, ii sunt fílii Abrahæ.
L.xq0: ^8^ Próvidens autem Scriptúra quia ex fide iustíficat gentes Deus, prænuntiávit Abrahæ: Quia benedicéntur in te omnes gentes.
L.xzo: ^9^ Igitur qui ex fide sunt, benedicéntur cum fidéli Abraham.
L.s72: ^10^ Quicúmque enim ex opéribus legis sunt, sub maledícto sunt. Scriptum est enim: Maledíctus omnis qui non permánserit in ómnibus quæ scripta sunt in libro legis ut fáciat ea.
L.sh0: ^11^ Quóniam autem in lege nemo iustificátur apud Deum, maniféstum est: quia iustus ex fide vivit.
L.sor: ^12^ Lex autem non est ex fide, sed: Qui fécerit ea, vivet in illis.
L.suf: ^13^ Christus nos redémit de maledícto legis, factus pro nobis maledíctum: quia scriptum est: Maledíctus omnis qui pendet in ligno:
L.t6o: ^14^ Ut in géntibus benedíctio Abrahæ fíeret in Christo Iesu, ut pollicitatiónem Spíritus accipiámus per fidem.
L.xcs: ^7^ Know ye therefore, that they who are of faith, the same are the children of Abraham.
L.xjl: ^8^ And the scripture, foreseeing, that God justifieth the Gentiles by faith, told unto Abraham before: In thee shall all nations be blessed.
L.y3f: ^9^ Therefore they that are of faith, shall be blessed with faithful Abraham.
L.s3v: ^10^ For as many as are of the works of the law, are under a curse. For it is written: Cursed is every one, that abideth not in all things, which are written in the book of the law to do them.
L.sbq: ^11^ But that in the law no man is justified with God, it is manifest: because the just man liveth by faith.
L.slj: ^12^ But the law is not of faith: but, He that doth those things, shall live in them.
L.sue: ^13^ Christ hath redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us: for it is written: Cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree:
L.t67: ^14^ That the blessing of Abraham might come on the Gentiles through Christ Jesus: that we may receive the promise of the Spirit by faith.
L.r0h: Timótheus, Lystris in Lycaónia natus ex patre gentíli et matre iudǽa, christiánam colébat religiónem, cum in ea loca venit Paulus Apóstolus. Qui fama commótus, quæ de Timóthei sanctitáte percrebúerat, ipsum adhíbuit sócium suæ peregrinatiónis: sed propter Iudǽos qui se ad Christum convérterant, sciéntes Timóthei patrem esse gentílem, eum circumcídit. Cum ígitur ambo Ephesum veníssent, ibi ordinátus est epíscopus ab Apóstolo, ut eam ecclésiam gubernáret. Ad quem Apóstolus duas epístolas scripsit, álteram Laodicéa, álteram Roma. Quibus in pastorális offícii cura confirmátus, cum sacrifícium, quod uni Deo debétur fíeri dǽmonum simulácris, ferre non posset; pópulum Ephesínum, Diánæ in eius celebritáte immolántem, ab illa impietáte removére conátus, lapídibus óbrutus est; ac pene mórtuus, a Christiánis eréptus et in montem óppido vicínum delátus, nono caléndas februárii obdormívit in Dómino.
L.r0f: Timothy was born in Lystra in Lycaonia of a gentile father and a Jewish mother, and was a follower of the Christian religion when the Apostle Paul visited that city. Paul was so moved by what he repeatedly heard of Timothy's holiness that he took him with him as a companion on his journeys; yet, because of the Jews who had been converted to Christ and who knew that Timothy's father had been a Gentile, he had him circumcised. When they both arrived at Ephesus, the Apostle ordained him bishop to govern the Church there. The Apostle wrote him two letters, one from Laodicea, the other from Rome. Strengthened by these letters in the ministry of his pastoral office, he could not endure that the sacrifice which is due to God alone should be offered to the images of demons, and he strove to win over the people of Ephesus from the impiety of offering sacrifice to Diana on her feast day. He was stoned, and was nearly dead when the Christians rescued him and took him to a village on a neighboring mountain. There he died in the Lord on January 24.
L.b08: Infirmitátem nostram réspice, omnípotens Deus: et, quia pondus própriæ actiónis gravat, beáti Timóthei Mártyris tui atque Pontíficis intercéssio gloriósa nos prótegat.
L.bay: Mercifully consider our weakness, O Almighty God, and whereas by the burden of our sins we are sore, may the glorious intercession of blessed Timothy, Your Martyr and Bishop, sustain us.
L.nfg: Incipit Epístola beáti Pauli Apóstoli ad Ephésios
L.u1f: ^1^ Paulus Apóstolus Iesu Christi per voluntátem Dei, ómnibus sanctis qui sunt Ephesi, et fidélibus in Christo Iesu.
L.vjh: ^3^ Benedíctus Deus et Pater Dómini nostri Iesu Christi, qui benedíxit nos in omni benedictióne spirituáli in cæléstibus in Christo,
L.w81: ^4^ Sicut elégit nos in ipso ante mundi constitutiónem, ut essémus sancti et immaculáti in conspéctu eius in caritáte.
L.u1a: ^1^ Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ, by the will of God, to all the saints who are at Ephesus, and to the faithful in Christ Jesus.
L.v2r: ^2^ Grace be to you, and peace from God the Father, and from the Lord Jesus Christ.
L.vjk: ^3^ Blessed by the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who hath blessed us with spiritual blessings in heavenly places, in Christ:
L.w09: ^4^ As he chose us in him before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy and unspotted in his sight in charity.
L.wp4: ^5^ Qui prædestinávit nos in adoptiónem filiórum per Iesum Christum in ipsum: secúndum propósitum voluntátis suæ,
L.x07: ^6^ In laudem glóriæ grátiæ suæ, in qua gratificávit nos in dilécto Fílio suo.
L.xcg: ^7^ In quo habémus redemptiónem per sánguinem eius, remissiónem peccatórum secúndum divítias grátiæ eius,
L.xqj: ^8^ Quæ superabundávit in nobis in omni sapiéntia et prudéntia:
L.y3w: ^9^ Ut notum fáceret nobis sacraméntum voluntátis suæ, secúndum beneplácitum eius, quod propósuit in eo,
L.s4y: ^10^ In dispensatióne plenitúdinis témporum, instauráre ómnia in Christo, quæ in cælis et quæ in terra sunt, in ipso;
L.sfc: ^11^ In quo étiam et nos sorte vocáti sumus prædestináti secúndum propósitum eius qui operátur ómnia secúndum consílium voluntátis suæ:
L.sry: ^12^ Ut simus in laudem glóriæ eius nos, qui ante sperávimus in Christo;
L.swx: ^13^ In quo et vos, cum audissétis verbum veritátis, Evangélium salútis vestræ, in quo et credéntes signáti estis Spíritu promissiónis Sancto,
L.t59: ^14^ Qui est pignus hereditátis nostræ, in redemptiónem acquisitiónis, in laudem glóriæ ipsíus.
L.wrn: ^5^ Who hath predestinated us unto the adoption of children through Jesus Christ unto himself: according to the purpose of his will:
L.x4n: ^6^ Unto the praise of the glory of his grace, in which he hath graced us in his beloved son.
L.xcl: ^7^ In whom we have redemption through his blood, the remission of sins, according to the riches of his grace,
L.xst: ^8^ Which hath superabounded in us in all wisdom and prudence,
L.y34: ^9^ That he might make known unto us the mystery of his will, according to his good pleasure, which he hath purposed in him,
L.s52: ^10^ In the dispensation of the fulness of times, to re-establish all things in Christ, that are in heaven and on earth, in him.
L.sff: ^11^ In whom we also are called by lot, being predestinated according to the purpose of him who worketh all things according to the counsel of his will.
L.sr3: ^12^ That we may be unto the praise of his glory, we who before hoped Christ:
L.sx3: ^13^ In whom you also, after you had heard the word of truth, (the gospel of your salvation;) in whom also believing, you were signed with the holy Spirit of promise,
L.t70: ^14^ Who is the pledge of our inheritance, unto the redemption of acquisition, unto the praise of his glory.
L.u0p: ^1^ Obsecro ítaque vos ego vinctus in Dómino, ut digne ambulétis vocatióne, qua vocáti estis,
L.uzo: ^2^ Cum omni humilitáte, et mansuetúdine, cum patiéntia, supportántes ínvicem in caritáte,
L.vqw: ^3^ Sollíciti serváre unitátem Spíritus in vínculo pacis.
L.w9i: ^4^ Unum corpus, et unus Spíritus, sicut vocáti estis in una spe vocatiónis vestræ.
L.wrc: ^5^ Unus Dóminus, una fides, unum baptísma.
L.x4o: ^6^ Unus Deus et Pater ómnium, qui est super omnes, et per ómnia, et in ómnibus nobis.
L.tya: ^1^ I therefore, a prisoner in the Lord, beseech you that you walk worthy of the vocation in which you are called,
L.v8d: ^2^ With all humility and mildness, with patience, supporting one another in charity.
L.vjt: ^3^ Careful to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace.
L.w6i: ^4^ One body and one Spirit; as you are called in one hope of your calling.
L.woj: ^5^ One Lord, one faith, one baptism.
L.x1z: ^6^ One God and Father of all, who is above all, and through all, and in us all.
L.xgo: ^7^ Unicuíque autem nostrum data est grátia secúndum mensúram donatiónis Christi.
L.xpu: ^8^ Propter quod dicit: Ascéndens in altum, captívam duxit captivitátem: dedit dona homínibus.
L.y21: ^9^ Quod autem ascéndit, quid est, nisi quia et descéndit primum in inferióres partes terræ?
L.s6t: ^10^ Qui descéndit, ipse est et qui ascéndit super omnes cælos, ut impléret ómnia.
L.sdc: ^11^ Et ipse dedit quosdam quidem apóstolos, quosdam autem prophétas, álios vero evangelístas, álios autem pastóres et doctóres,
L.sk0: ^12^ Ad consummatiónem sanctórum in opus ministérii, in ædificatiónem córporis Christi:
L.sux: ^13^ Donec occurrámus omnes in unitátem fídei, et agnitiónis Fílii Dei, in virum perféctum, in mensúram ætátis plenitúdinis Christi:
L.t6n: ^14^ Ut iam non simus párvuli fluctuántes, et circumferámur omni vento doctrínæ in nequítia hóminum, in astútia ad circumventiónem erróris.
L.tcc: ^15^ Veritátem autem faciéntes in caritáte, crescámus in illo per ómnia, qui est caput Christus:
L.x8z: ^7^ But to every one of us is given grace, according to the measure of the giving of Christ.
L.xsr: ^8^ Wherefore he saith: Ascending on high, he led captivity captive; he gave gifts to men.
L.y11: ^9^ Now that he ascended, what is it, but because he also descended first into the lower parts of the earth?
L.s4i: ^10^ He that descended is the same also that ascended above all the heavens, that he might fill all things.
L.sa7: ^11^ And he gave some apostles, and some prophets, and other some evangelists, and other some pastors and doctors,
L.snh: ^12^ For the perfecting of the saints, for the work of the ministry, for the edifying of the body of Christ:
L.szs: ^13^ Until we all meet into the unity of faith, and of the knowledge of the Son of God, unto a perfect man, unto the measure of the age of the fulness of Christ;
L.t66: ^14^ That henceforth we be no more children tossed to and fro, and carried about with every wind of doctrine by the wickedness of men, by cunning craftiness, by which they lie in wait to deceive
L.t8d: ^15^ But doing the truth in charity, we may in all things grow up in him who is the head, even Christ:
L.twh: ^1^ Estóte ergo imitatóres Dei, sicut fílii caríssimi,
L.v0m: ^2^ Et ambuláte in dilectióne, sicut et Christus diléxit nos, et trádidit semetípsum pro nobis, oblatiónem et hóstiam Deo in odórem suavitátis.
L.vn1: ^3^ Fornicátio autem, et omnis immundítia, aut avarítia, nec nominétur in vobis, sicut decet sanctos:
L.w0f: ^4^ Aut turpitúdo, aut stultilóquium, aut scurrílitas, quæ ad rem non pértinet: sed magis gratiárum áctio.
L.tut: ^1^ Be ye therefore followers of God, as most dear children;
L.uyf: ^2^ And walk in love, as Christ also hath loved us, and hath delivered himself for us, an oblation and a sacrifice to God for an odour of sweetness.
L.vjn: ^3^ But fornication, and all uncleanness, or covetousness, let it not so much as be named among you, as becometh saints:
L.w6n: ^4^ Or obscenity, or foolish talking, or scurrility, which is to no purpose; but rather giving of thanks.
L.wm5: ^5^ Hoc enim scitóte intellegéntes: quod omnis fornicátor, aut immúndus, aut avárus, quod est idolórum sérvitus, non habet hereditátem in regno Christi et Dei.
L.x19: ^6^ Nemo vos sedúcat inánibus verbis: propter hæc enim venit ira Dei in fílios diffidéntiæ.
L.xlw: ^8^ Erátis enim aliquándo ténebræ: nunc autem lux in Dómino. Ut fílii lucis ambuláte:
L.xyw: ^9^ Fructus enim lucis est in omni bonitáte, et iustítia, et veritáte:
L.sdg: ^11^ Et nolíte communicáre opéribus infructuósis tenebrárum, magis autem redargúite.

L.ni1: Ioánnes Bosco, húmili loco natus, post ærumnósam innocentissimámque puerítiam, stúdiis Chérii óperam dedit, quo quidem témpore ingénii et virtútum laude enítuit. Sacérdos creátus, Augústam Taurinórum pétiit, ubi ómnibus ómnia factus est; sed præsértim in adolescéntulos eósque páuperes ac derelíctos adiuvándos curam impéndit. Liberálibus disciplínis, opifícum scholis, festórum diérum ascetériis a venenátis errórum vitiorúmque pábulis puerílem ætátem removére omni ope stúduit: quam ad rem duas in Ecclésia virórum virginúmque famílias excitávit. Plúrimos ipse édidit libros christiána sapiéntia refértos. De ætérna étiam infidélium salúte per sacras suórum sodálium expeditiónes óptime méruit. Mente in Deum constánter erécta, nullis homo sanctíssimus, nec minis terréri, nec labóribus fatigári, nec curis ópprimi, nec rebus advérsis perturbári videbátur. Obiit anno salútis millésimo octingentésimo octogésimo octávo, ætátis septuagésimo tértio. A Pio undécimo, Pontífice máximo, in Sanctórum númerum relátus est.
L.qru: The childhood of Don Bosco, who was born in a small village was marked both by its hardship and by his happy innocence of soul. He studied at Chieri, where in a short time he earned great praise for his brilliance and his virtue. Ordained priest, he went to Turin, where he made himself all things to all men, and undertook in particular the work of aiding poor and neglected boys. By providing them with teaching in the liberal arts and in trades and keeping them occupied on holidays, he strove with all his might to remove young people from poisonous sources of delinquency and vice. For this purpose, he established two congregations in the Church, one for men and one for women religious. He himself published many books filled with Christian wisdom. He also accomplished great things for the eternal salvation of unbelievers through the missionary enterprises of his congregations. With his mind constantly raised to God, this holy man never seemed to be terrified by threats, worn out by labors, oppressed by cares, or disturbed by adversities. He died in the year of salvation 1888 at the age of seventy-three, and was numbered among the Saints by Pope Pius XI.
L.a4y: Deus, qui sanctum Ioánnem Confessórem tuum adolescéntium patrem et magístrum excitásti, ac per eum, auxiliatríce Vírgine María, novas in Ecclésia tua famílias floréscere voluísti: concéde, quǽsumus; ut eódem caritátis igne succénsi, ánimas quǽrere, tibíque soli servíre valeámus.
L.bir: O God, who didst raise up thy blessed Confessor John, to be a father and teacher of youth, and didst will that through him, with the help of the Virgin Mary, new families should flourish in the Church, grant we pray that enkindled with the same fire of charity we may be strong to seek after souls and to serve thee alone.
